Also, MS NOW spoke to military families who described a harrowing evacuation from a naval base in Bahrain. MS NOW Pentagon Reporter Priya Sridhar has more details. Democratic strategist Dan Kanninen and retired U.S. Army Brigadier General Steven Anderson join Alicia Menendez to share their thoughts.

The British Police Rearrest Two in Connection With Alleged Terror Plot — The counterterrorism police investigating a threat against an English air base used by U.S. bombers said the two men were working on behalf of Iran.

News Wrap: Britain sending air support to Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks — In our news wrap Tuesday, British authorities say they're sending air support to Saudi Arabia to protect against missiles and drones launched by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen, Vice President Vance says he's not endorsing Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israeli elections and voters in Alberta overwhelmingly rejected a referendum that would have put the province on a path toward independence.

Yemeni City of Taiz Running Out of Essentials as Houthis Close in — The Iranian-backed Houthi militia has cut road access to Taiz, one of Yemen’s largest cities, besieging it. Officials there warn of an impending humanitarian disaster.

Sea mine crisis re-emerges in Strait of Hormuz as Tehran urges Washington to accept deal — Iran claims two oil tankers struck sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz as the IMO warns the critical shipping lane remains too unsafe to transit.

UK to Send Fighter Jets to Help Defend Saudi Arabia From Houthi Attacks — R.A.F. Typhoon fighter jets will be deployed to protect infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, Britain said, after a spike in attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi militia.

Iran regime under pressure as rebel groups escalate attacks in volatile southeast — A coalition of armed rebel groups is stepping up attacks against Iranian regime forces in the country's volatile southeast, raising questions about Tehran's grip on the region.
